ambiguities.description: The text does not define eligibility criteria for 'low-income' participants (e.g., an income threshold or benefit-program proxy), which determines recruitment scope and enrollment targets a bidder must price and staff.

It is unclear whether a bidder may propose for both tracks under a single contract or must submit separate proposals per track, and whether the 'up to two (2)' awards means one administrator per track.

The text does not define what counts as "low-income" for student eligibility, nor how many students must be served or how many internship placements must be secured; a bidder would ask for the eligibility threshold and the required cohort/placement scale to size the program and price it.

The text does not specify the stipend amount, duration, or whether internship wages are paid by the administrator or the host employer; a bidder would ask who funds stipends and internship pay and at what rate.

The text does not specify the stipend amount, duration, or how much of the $2M per-track cap must be allocated to stipends versus training delivery, which materially changes the budget model; the bidder would ask what stipend level and share of the award are expected.

The program must be 'immersive' and deliverable part-time or full-time, but neither the total training hours nor the minimum/maximum program duration per participant is defined; the bidder would ask what intensity and length constitute an acceptable immersive schedule.

The text sets a 250-participant minimum as a "should" while giving priority to applicants serving more than 400, leaving unclear whether 250 is a pass/fail threshold or merely a scored preference. The bidder would ask how participant counts are scored and whether a proposal below 250 is disqualified.

"The majority of graduates" and "closely related field" are undefined, and no measurement period or verification method is given, so the bidder cannot tell what outcome commitment it is making. The bidder would ask what percentage and time frame define success and how employment outcomes are documented.

The low-income threshold is marked with a footnote reference that is not included in this text, so the definition of "low-income" is unknown. The bidder would ask which income definition or eligibility standard applies.

The RFP does not say how experience in a domain is demonstrated or measured (e.g., years of experience, number of students served, contract values), so a bidder cannot tell whether its track record qualifies or what evidence to submit.

The text refers to "one track" and "both tracks" without defining what the tracks are or how many exist, which determines whether the $2M or $4M cap applies; the bidder would ask how many tracks the program has and what each covers.

ESD may deny reimbursement of expenses it deems ineligible, but the text does not state which expense categories are eligible; the bidder would ask for the eligible cost categories or a cost manual governing reimbursement.

The budget must be "mapped to the program duration," but the program duration is not stated in this text; the bidder would ask what the grant period length is and whether the budget must be broken out by month, quarter or year.
The participant stipend level is a required budget line but no cap, per-participant amount or eligible use is given here; the bidder would ask what stipend range or ceiling applies.

The text says there is no cost-match requirement but that cost-matching earns additional points, without stating how much match is needed or how points scale. A bidder would ask what match percentage or amount maximizes scoring and whether any minimum is expected.

The chunk refers to "Proposed definition" without stating what definition is being proposed or what criteria an alternative must meet. A bidder would ask which definition this refers to and what justification standard applies.

The exact list of data points is left to ESD and will only be fixed during contract negotiation, so the bidder cannot know the full reporting scope or effort to price; the bidder would ask for the definitive data-point list and reporting frequency/format.

The text does not define how 'low-income' is determined (e.g., income threshold or program eligibility criterion), which affects data collection design; the bidder would ask for the definition to apply.

The Corporation reserves the right to change any of the dates, so the bidder cannot rely on the stated schedule; the bidder would ask whether the submission deadline and contract start date are firm or subject to change and how changes will be communicated.
The anticipated debriefing timeframe is listed as TBD, leaving the post-award schedule open; the bidder would ask when debriefings will occur.

The college-student and other-participant items ask for cost per student/participant and placement rates but do not define the reporting period or whether figures are per cohort or cumulative, so a bidder cannot tell which numbers to report.

The phrase "if not already addressed" leaves it unclear whether the employer-coordination and New York items may be omitted when covered elsewhere in the proposal, or must be cross-referenced explicitly.

The text requires a monthly timeline running through completion of internships or full-time jobs by the first cohort but gives no cohort start date or program period, so the bidder cannot anchor the schedule; the bidder would ask for the intended program start date and the required end date for the first cohort.

The proposal must state a proposed stipend level and/or other supports, but the text does not say whether a stipend is required, what it must cover, or whether it is subject to a cap; the bidder would ask whether stipends are mandatory and whether any funding ceiling applies.

The text does not define "low-income participants" (e.g., which income threshold or eligibility standard applies), which determines the denominator for the completion-rate metric and thus the commitment the bidder makes; the bidder would ask which definition or standard to use.

It is unclear whether the placement rate is measured at graduation, within a set period after graduation, or over a defined tracking window, and whether paid internships must meet a minimum duration; the bidder would ask for the measurement period and definition of placement.

The bracketed note says a uniform schedule of all fee components should be established "in case of complex cost structure" but does not define what counts as complex or what the schedule must look like; the bidder would ask whether a prescribed cost schedule template exists and when it is required.

The Technical Proposal must include a "Cost of Services" section, yet pricing is normally submitted separately; bidders would ask whether cost information belongs in the technical volume or a separate price proposal, and whether including it risks disclosure.

The "Diversity Practices Questionnaire" is listed as required content but is not provided in this text; bidders would ask where the questionnaire form is obtained and whether it is a separate document.

The text says failure to submit any listed requirement "may result in the rejection" of the proposal, leaving it unclear whether any omission is disqualifying or curable; a bidder would ask whether missing items can be supplied after submission and whether the order of items is strictly enforced.

The chunk states that late proposals will not be considered but gives no submission deadline or time zone; the bidder would ask for the exact due date and time and whether the Dropbox upload timestamp governs receipt.
The folder naming convention requires the "date of Submission" but does not specify a date format (the example uses MM.DD.YYYY); the bidder would ask which format is required.

The text says OSC approval "may be required" for contracts over one million dollars paid with State monies or awarded non-competitively, so it is unclear whether this procurement will actually be subject to OSC review and how long that approval could delay contract execution; a bidder would ask whether OSC approval applies here and what schedule impact to assume.

The contract requires performance "in a timely and professional manner" and assessment via progress reports and periodic meetings, but no reporting frequency, format or meeting cadence is defined here; a bidder would ask how often progress reports and meetings are expected so it can staff and price the effort.

"Applicable professional standards" is not defined, and the no-charge correction obligation is limited to errors in "the progression of its work"; a bidder would ask which standards apply and how long the correction obligation lasts after delivery.

The clause allows the Corporation to accept a claim asserted after the 30-day window if it decides the facts justify it, so it is unclear whether the 30-day deadline is a hard bar or waivable; a bidder would ask how strictly the deadline is enforced.

The Corporation has "absolute right and discretion" to approve or disapprove staff changes, yet approval "shall not be unreasonably withheld"; bidders would ask which standard governs and what criteria or timeline apply to approval decisions.
The Contractor must notify the Corporation of staff changes "immediately", but no notice period or approval lead time is defined, so bidders cannot plan staffing transitions or schedule risk.

The text allows subcontracting that is "indicated in its proposal" without prior written approval, but does not say how much detail the proposal must give about subcontractors or whether such disclosure still requires later approval; a bidder would ask what subcontractor information must be included in the proposal.

The disclosure obligation refers to relationships with "former officers and employees of ESD" without saying how far back or which former personnel must be covered, so a bidder cannot tell what it must search for and disclose; the bidder would ask what look-back period and scope of former ESD personnel applies.

The text refers to conflicts "enumerated in this RFP" but the enumeration is not in this chunk, so a bidder cannot tell which relationships or situations must be screened and disclosed; the bidder would ask which conflicts are enumerated and where.

The text refers to "the designated contact persons listed above" without naming them in this chunk, so a bidder cannot tell whom it may lawfully contact during the Restricted Period; the bidder would ask for the names and contact details of the designated contacts.

The requirement for "periodic updating of such forms" does not state the frequency or triggering events for updates; the bidder would ask how often, and upon what events, the forms must be refreshed during the contract term.

The chunk refers to "the forms required above" without naming them in this text; a bidder would ask which specific forms (and whether separate copies are needed per sub-consultant) must be submitted and where in the proposal they belong.

The text says the Respondent must remain "responsible" throughout the contract term and that ESD may suspend or terminate if responsibility is questioned, but it does not define what ongoing reporting or notification obligations the vendor has; a bidder would ask what ongoing responsibility certifications or updates are required during the term.

The 30 percent MWBE participation goal is stated as an overall goal, but it is unclear whether a respondent must meet it or only demonstrate good faith efforts toward it, and whether the goal applies to the total contract value or to subcontracting spend; a bidder would ask which basis is used and whether a shortfall is disqualifying.

The text requires 'the required MWBE documentation' without specifying which forms or submissions are needed and when they are due, so a bidder cannot tell what to file with its response versus after award; the bidder would ask for the list of required MWBE documents and their deadlines.

The text refers to "the MWBE participation goals set forth in a Contract resulting from this RFP" but does not state the numeric goals in this chunk; a bidder would ask what the applicable MWBE participation percentages are.

The 25 percent broker rule applies "FOR ALL OTHER CONTRACTS" without defining which contract categories are excluded or what qualifies as a broker arrangement; a bidder would ask whether this rule applies to its contract type.
The text requires a written remedy that is "timely" and not "inadequate" without defining either standard; a bidder would ask what content and level of detail ESD considers an adequate remedy.

The equal employment opportunity program obligation is scoped to subcontracts for construction, demolition, repair, renovation, planning or design of real property, which may not match an AI services contract; the bidder would ask whether this requirement applies to its scope of work at all.
The Workforce Utilization Report format is left to ESD to specify and is not provided here; the bidder would ask when the required format and reporting portal will be made available.

The text lists six OCSD forms as "required" but does not say which must be submitted with the proposal versus maintained or filed during contract performance (e.g., the quarterly Workforce Utilization Report or a waiver request). A bidder would ask which forms are due at submission and which are ongoing obligations.

The text says SDVOB participation is "expected" but sets no goal percentage, reporting form, or evidence of good-faith effort, so a bidder cannot tell whether any SDVOB utilization must be documented in the proposal or priced into the subcontracting plan.

The text sets an overall goal of 6% SDVOB participation but does not state whether that percentage applies to total contract value, subcontracting dollars, or another base, nor whether it is a pass/fail requirement; a bidder would ask how the 6% is measured and what happens if it is not met.

"Good faith efforts" is undefined in this text, so a bidder cannot know what documentation (e.g., solicitations issued, responses received, reasons for rejection) will satisfy the requirement; the bidder would ask for the required form and evidence standard.

The Utilization Plan must describe work performed "to meet the goals on the Contract", but no SDVOB participation goal percentage or dollar target appears in this text, so a bidder cannot tell what level of SDVOB participation is required or how it will be judged.

The text refers to "the prescribed SDVOB contract goals set forth above" without stating the numeric goal in this chunk, so a bidder cannot tell what SDVOB participation percentage it must commit to in the Utilization Plan.
The standard for an "inadequate" written remedy or "good faith efforts" is not defined here, so a bidder cannot know what level of documentation will satisfy ESD and avoid disqualification.

The text refers to 'the goal requirements, as set forth in clause IV below' and to 'clauses II (C), (D) & (E)', but those clauses are not included in this chunk, so the applicable MWBE/SDVOB participation goals and the consequences of a rejected waiver are unknown; the bidder would ask what the goals are and what happens if a waiver submitted with the Utilization Plan is not accepted.

The text mixes MWBE and SDVOB terminology (the section title covers minority- and women-owned businesses, while the waiver is filed on Form OCSD-5 and tied to the SDVOB Utilization Plan), leaving unclear which goal set the waiver applies to and whether separate waivers are needed; the bidder would ask for clarification.

The text refers to "established goal requirements" and SDVOB contract goals without stating the goal percentages or the scope of the SDVOB Utilization Plan obligations in this chunk; a bidder would ask what specific MWBE/SDVOB participation goals apply and what the waiver criteria are.

The chunk requires documentation of good faith efforts toward SDVOB utilization and refers to a "waiver request", but it does not state whether a waiver of the SDVOB goals is being sought, what the SDVOB participation goal percentage is, or whether these documents are submitted with the proposal or during contract performance. A bidder would ask what the SDVOB goal is and when and to whom the good faith effort documentation must be submitted.

The SDVOB participation goals and the damages payable for non-compliance are said to be "set forth in the Contract" but are not stated here; the bidder would ask what the specific goal percentages and damage amounts are.

The text does not state how often the STL 5-a certifications in Form ST-220-CA must be updated during the contract, so the bidder cannot plan the administrative effort or cost; the bidder would ask what the required update frequency is.

It is unclear whether the affidavit alternative (STL5A-Affidavit) may be used by any Respondent or only by those not required to register, and whether it must be accompanied by Form ST-220-CA; the bidder would ask which document set satisfies the requirement in its circumstances.

The text requires concerns about Schedule A to be submitted "in a timely manner" but sets no deadline, and failure to do so waives objections; a bidder would ask what date or interval constitutes timely submission.

The insurance list is qualified as applying "at a minimum and to the extent applicable", so it is unclear which coverages (e.g., Commercial Automobile, Sexual Abuse and Molestation) a bidder without vehicles or without relevant exposure must still carry; the bidder would ask which policies are mandatory for its specific scope.

The waiver of subrogation is stated with "should" while the other insurance terms are mandatory, so it is unclear whether the waiver is a firm contract condition or merely preferred; the bidder would ask whether it is required at award.

Conflicting requirements R114 and R103: R114 forbids including any information beyond what is specifically requested, while R103 requires the proposal to provide all information requested and R104 emphasizes completeness, which pull in opposite directions on how much content to include.

Conflicting requirements R258 and R259: R258 forbids including Schedule A information/documentation in the proposal submission, while R259 requires submitting written concerns about Schedule A terms together with the Administrative Proposal.
